arxiv-2102-03867.title: Positional Marked Patterns in Permutations
arxiv-2102-03867.creator: Sittipong Thamrongpairoj, Jeffrey B. Remmel
arxiv-2102-03867.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sittipong Thamrongpairoj, Jeffrey B. Remmel. We introduce the notion of positional marked pattern, which is a permutation τ \displaystyle\tau with one element underlined. Given a permutation σ \displaystyle\sigma , we say that σ \displaystyle\sigma has a τ \displaystyle\tau -match at position i \displaystyle i if τ \displaystyle\tau occurs in σ \displaystyle\sigma in such a way that σ i \displaystyle\sigma_{i} plays the role of the underlined element in the occurrence.

arxiv-2402-13867.title: RFI-DRUnet: Restoring dynamic spectra corrupted by radio frequency interference – Application to pulsar observations Journal: Submitted to a journal
arxiv-2402-13867.creator: Xiao Zhang, Ismaël Cognard, Nicolas Dobigeon
arxiv-2402-13867.description: Abstract Radio frequency interference (RFI) have been an enduring concern in radio astronomy, particularly for the observations of pulsars which require high timing precision and data sensitivity. In most works of the literature, RFI mitigation has been formulated as a detection task that consists of localizing possible RFI in dynamic spectra.

arxiv-2406-07981.title: Towards Accelerating Real-Time Path Tracing with Foveated Framework
arxiv-2406-07981.creator: Bipul Mohanto 1 , Sven Kluge 1 , and Oliver Staadt 1 1 University of Rostock, Institute of Visual and Analytic Computing, Germany
arxiv-2406-07981.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Bipul Mohanto 1 , Sven Kluge 1 , and Oliver Staadt 1 1 University of Rostock, Institute of Visual and Analytic Computing, Germany. Path tracing is one of the most widespread rendering techniques for high-end graphics fidelity. However, the slow convergence time and presence of intensive noises make it infeasible for numerous real-time applications where physically corrected photorealistic effects are salient.

arxiv-2510-20465.title: An interpretable molecular descriptor for machine learning predictions in atmospheric science
arxiv-2510-20465.creator: L. Lind, H. Sandström, P. Rinke
arxiv-2510-20465.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by L. Lind, H. Sandström, P. Rinke. The study of aerosol formation and chemistry using machine learning is limited by the lack of molecular descriptors suited to atmospheric compounds. Interpretable models are particularly affected because they often rely on dictionary-based descriptors tied to specific molecular substructures, which currently fail to capture the full range of organic atmospheric compounds, including large, highly oxidized molecules common in the atmosphere.

arxiv-2601-02316.title: DatBench Discriminative, Faithful, and Efficient VLM Evaluations
arxiv-2601-02316.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by . Empirical evaluation serves as the primary compass guiding research progress in foundation models. Despite a large body of work focused on training frontier vision-language models (VLMs), approaches to their evaluation remain nascent. To guide their maturation, we propose three desiderata that evaluations should satisfy: (1) faithfulness to the modality and application, (2) discriminability between models of varying quality, and (3) efficiency in compute.

britannica-1911-augsburg.title: Augsburg (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-augsburg.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-augsburg.description: Article 'Augsburg' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 2), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Augsburg (the Augusta Vindelicorum of the Romans) derives its name from the Roman emperor Augustus, who, on the conquest of Rhaetia by Drusus, established here a Roman colony about 14 B.C. In the 5th century it was sacked by the Huns, and afterwards came under the power of the Frankish kings.

britannica-1911-moonstone.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-moonstone.description: Article 'Moonstone' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 18), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. a bluish opalescence, whence its value as an ornamental stone. When cut with a convex surface it displays a soft milky reflection, forming a luminous band, but not sharply defined as in cat’s-eye.

eymerich-directorium-inquisitorum-1578-l.creator: Nicholas Eymerich
eymerich-directorium-inquisitorum-1578-l.description: Eymerich's Directorium Inquisitorum (1376) in the 1578 Rome edition with Francisco Peña's commentaries — the inquisitor's handbook for two centuries, with the witchcraft and sorcery sections that fed the Malleus tradition. pmc-10537815.title: Implication of different frailty criteria in older people with atrial fibrillation: a prospective cohort study
pmc-10537815.creator: Junpeng Liu, Ke Chai, Wanrong Zhu, Minghui DU, Chen Meng, Lin Yang, Lingling Cui, Di Guo, Ning Sun, Hua Wang, Jiefu Yang
pmc-10537815.description: Backgroundthe prevalence of physical and multidimensional frailty and their prognostic impact on clinical outcomes in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) is unclear.Objectiveto evaluated frailty in a cohort of patients with AF according to different criteria, and studied the prevalence and its prognostic impact on clinical outcomes.

pmc-11420196.title: The roles of geometry and viscosity in the mobilization of coarse sediment by finer sediment
pmc-11420196.creator: Marwan A. Hassan, Gary Parker, Yarra Hassan, Chenge An, Xudong Fu, Jeremy G. Venditti
pmc-11420196.description: SignificanceIn gravel-sand rivers, coarser sediment is heavier and thus more difficult to move. It has been observed that additions of fine sediment can increase the mobility of coarse sediment. This effect can disrupt the riverbed stability and further affect infrastructure safety and aquatic habitat.

pmc-11709808.title: Repurposing drugs that slow down aging for the prevention of Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11709808.creator: Simone Tambaro, Andrea Mosqueda Solis, Bowen Tang, Thais Lopes De Oliveira, Chenxi Qin, Alan Kavsek, Arvid Sjölander, Kristina Johnell, Dorota Religa, Christian Riedel, Per Nilsson, Sara Hägg
pmc-11709808.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundHigh age is the biggest risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Approved drugs that slow down the aging process have the potential to be repurposed for the primary prevention of AD. pmc-12433656.title: Emotional Lability Independently Predicts Functional Impairment in Children with ADHD: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-12433656.creator: Xiaolan Cao, Zhaomin Wu, Juan Liu, Ying Li, Linlin Zhang, Yufeng Wang, Binrang Yang
pmc-12433656.description: BackgroundEmotional lability (EL), characterized by excessive emotional fluctuations and intense outbursts, frequently co-occurs with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and may exacerbate functional impairments. This study aimed to explore the disparities in ADHD-related symptoms and functional impairments in children with ADHD who exhibited EL and those without it and to examine the unique contribution of EL to functional impairments.

pmc-12509166.title: Optimising knowledge mobilisation for mental health research in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review of the state of knowledge and directions for future research
pmc-12509166.creator: Cintia Faija, Penny Bee, Rebecca Pedley, Mia Bennion, Herni Susanti, Fitri Fausiah, Sri Idaiani, Dwie Susilo, Mohammad Hussen, Helen Brooks, Anonymous, Donald Kokonya, Anonymous, David Ndetei, Judith Bass, Donald Kokonya, Anonymous, David Ndetei, Judith Bass, Donald Kokonya, David Ndetei, Judith Bas
pmc-12509166.description: Keywords: mental health, knowledge mobilisation, low- and middle-income countries, dissemination, research impact Impact statement Recent increases in global mental health funding have led to a surge in research activity across low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), improving our understanding of mental illness and informing intervention priorities.

pmc-12530175.title: Size Control of Highly Monodisperse Citrate-Stabilized Magnetite Nanoparticles in Aqueous Media: The Role of Cerium Cations
pmc-12530175.creator: Karen Mejía-Carmona, Muriel F. Gustà, Pablo Guardia, Maria Chiara Spadaro, Jordi Arbiol, Víctor Puntes, Neus G. Bastús
pmc-12530175.description: Controlling the nucleation and growth of magnetite nanoparticles (NPs) via aqueous coprecipitation at room temperature is inherently challenging due to kinetic and thermodynamic constraints. Rapid pH increases trigger a burst nucleation event that depletes precursors before significant growth occurs, while NP surfaces are quickly passivated by water and hydroxyl ions, forming a dewetting barrier that impedes further growth.

pmc-12542488.title: Clinicopathological analysis of three cases of breast desmoid-type fibromatosis
pmc-12542488.creator: Qiong Li, Cancan Zou, Yanlin Chen, Muzi Li, Shuang Liang, Tianjing Yan
pmc-12542488.description: BackgroundBreast desmoid-type fibromatosis is a rare, locally aggressive but non-metastatic mesenchymal tumor according to WHO classification, characterized by spindle cell proliferation with irregular infiltrative borders. Its morphological overlap with other spindle cell lesions necessitates careful differential diagnosis. It’s worth noting that multifocal breast desmoid-type fibromatosis has not been reported.

pmc-12719622.title: Global Trends in MPOX Research (2014–2025): A Bibliometric Analysis and Overview
pmc-12719622.creator: Lulu Xie, Yimin Zhou, Xinyu Zhang, Tian Lan, Wenchao Sun
pmc-12719622.description: The 2022 global monkeypox outbreak fuelled a surge in related research. In this study, a bibliometric analysis of 2,076 monkeypox-related articles indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection (from January 2014 to June 2025) was performed, and VOSviewer was used to visualize keyword co-occurrence networks and collaboration patterns among countries and institutions.

pmc-12753880.title: Research progress of online monitoring techniques for dissolved gas analysis in insulating oil
pmc-12753880.creator: Hua Mao, Fangqiang Wang, Jie Wang, Zeyao Ma, Yan Wang, Rui Peng, Zhi Geng, Xinsheng Lan
pmc-12753880.description: Dissolved gas analysis (DGA) in insulating oil can achieve early warning of local discharge, overheating or arc failure in transformers. It can also quantitatively evaluate the aging degree of insulating equipment, providing a basis for formulating predictive maintenance strategies, so as to improve the reliability of power grid power supply.

pmc-12929090.title: Clinicians who think scapular dyskinesis is important are more likely to identify it in healthy individuals
pmc-12929090.creator: Oscar Vila-Dieguez, Abel Cazorla-Rey, Lori A. Michener
pmc-12929090.description: ObjectiveTo assess interrater reliability of the visual scapular dyskinesis test among physical therapists and examine how clinician beliefs influence classifications of healthy shoulders.Methods104 physical therapists (≥3 years of experience) rated five videos of healthy volunteers performing weighted arm elevations, using a Yes/No classification for scapular dyskinesis.

pmc-12971059.title: Reviews, expert opinions, consensus statements, position papers, protocols, and evidence-based guidelines: what are their roles in clinical practice?
pmc-12971059.creator: Francisco TUSTUMI, Lucia CALTHORPE, Felipe José Fernández COIMBRA, Adnan ALSEIDI
pmc-12971059.description: The growth of primary research in digestive surgery has led to an increasing need for structured interpretation and application to clinical practice. Guidance documents have become essential tools for decision-making. However, the terminology surrounding clinical guidance documents is frequently inconsistent, and different formats are often used interchangeably.

pmc-12976425.title: The APOL1 variant p.N264K is predicted to block ion flow by occluding a pore at the cell surface
pmc-12976425.creator: Verena Höffken, Lara Console, Niklas Nelde, Hermann Pavenstädt, Cesare Indiveri, Thomas Weide
pmc-12976425.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Based on a combination of in silico and cell biological analyses, this study suggests that the APOL1 variant p.N264K (M1) may prevent G2-mediated kidney toxicity by physically blocking ion flux. Introduction

Humans are protected against protozoal infections by African trypanosomes, because they are inactivated by the human serum protein apolipoprotein L1 (APOL1), except for the subspecies Trypanosoma brucei gambiense and rhodesiense, which cause human African sleeping sickness (human African trypanosomiasis, HAT) (Vanhamme et al, 2003; Perez-Morga et al, 2005).

pmc-13001285.title: “Cigarettes led me back to smoking tik”: lived experience perspectives on tobacco use during substance use treatment and recovery in South Africa
pmc-13001285.creator: Lorraine Samba Chiseya, Bronwyn Myers
pmc-13001285.description: IntroductionDespite the high prevalence of tobacco use among people with substance use disorder (SUD), tobacco cessation is not a routine part of SUD treatment in South Africa. No studies have explored how people receiving SUD treatment view the effects of tobacco use on SUD treatment or their barriers to tobacco cessation.

pmc-13008211.title: Trends in mortality rates for musculoskeletal and connective tissue diseases
pmc-13008211.creator: Chengzhuan Luo, Junsheng Jiang
pmc-13008211.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The burden of the musculoskeletal system and connective tissue poses a significant public health challenge in the United States. Musculoskeletal diseases and connective tissue diseases independently contribute to high morbidity and mortality rates. This study seeks to investigate mortality trends associated with the simultaneous occurrence of the musculoskeletal system and connective tissue among the US population over the period from 1999 to 2020.

pmc-13313504.title: Modeling immune responses to autologous and allogeneic human stem cell–derived islet grafts in vivo
pmc-13313504.creator: Camillo Bechi Genzano, Giorgia Zanetti, Qian Du, Daniel Traum, Deeksha Lahori, Grant M. Downes, Sakshi A. Bhatele, Xiaolan Ding, Kyle D. Apley, Rebuma Firdessa Fite, Matthew Ishahak, Enrique Eduardo Sanchez-Castro, Jeffrey R. Millman, Yiming Luo, Klaus H. Kaestner, Cory Berkland, Dieter Egli, Megan
pmc-13313504.description: Stem cell–derived β cells offer a promising approach for type 1 diabetes (T1D) treatment. However, the processes of graft infiltration and rejection by immune cells remain poorly understood in humans. In this study, autologous or allogeneic stem cell–derived islets (SC-islets) were transplanted in human immune system mice and analyzed 14 to 18 weeks later.

pmc-13359780.title: Divergent Evolutionary Profile of MULE Transposons in Arthropods
pmc-13359780.creator: Hong Chen, Shasha Shi, Kuilin Xiang, Quan Wang, Naisu Yang, Bo Gao, Chengyi Song
pmc-13359780.description: Simple SummaryThe evolutionary profiles of MULE transposons in arthropod genomes remain largely unknown. Analyzing 4268 genomes, we defined their distribution, diversity, structure, and activity. In total, 222 species harbor 322 distinct complete MULEs, whose transposases form twelve clades. Copy numbers range from 5 to 88, and lengths vary from 1.4 to 10.0 kb (mostly 2.5–5.0 kb).

pmc-13447070.title: Phosphorylation of tumour suppressor Amotl2 by IKBKE kinase promotes YAP1 signalling, enhancing glioblastoma growth
pmc-13447070.creator: Gaochao Guo, Yan Sun, Rujun Hong, Yalin Lu, Xingjie Chen, Liming Zhao, Chaoyue Li, Yang Liu, Qiang Huang

pmc-13528690.title: SemanticST: A Scalable Multi‐Contextual Graph Learning Framework for Uncovering Spatial Niches and Robust Multi‐Sample Integration in Spatial Transcriptomics
pmc-13528690.creator: Roxana Zahedi, Ahmadreza Argha, Nona Farbehi, Ivan Bakhshayeshi, Thantrira Porntaveetus, Youqiong Ye, Nigel H Lovell, Hamid Alinejad‐Rokny
pmc-13528690.description: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) analysis is often hindered by technical limitations and methodological biases that let dominant signals overshadow subtle but crucial biological patterns, such as rare cell types and fine‐grained heterogeneity. This is especially true for high‐complexity datasets from platforms like Xenium. We present SemanticST, a graph neural network (GNN) framework that addresses this challenge through a fundamentally different design.
